chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his forefathers, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:

Two men entered the mosque after the people had already prayed. So 'Ali عليه السلام said to them: “If you wish, let one of you lead his companion in prayer, but he should neither give the adhan nor the iqamah.”

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, the place where the prayer setting occurs
key_terms.صَاحِبَهُ: his companion, meaning the other person praying with him
key_terms.صَلَّى: performed prayer; here indicating that the people had already completed the congregational prayer
key_terms.فَلْيَؤُمَّ: let him lead in prayer as Imam
key_terms.يُقِيمُ: to pronounce the iqamah before prayer

ai.seo_question: If two people enter the mosque after the congregational prayer is over, may they pray together and repeat the adhan and iqamah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about two men arriving at the mosque after the congregational prayer has already been performed. Imam 'Ali عليه السلام permits them to pray together in congregation, but without repeating the adhan or the iqamah.
